page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a high base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 60 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, scoring 2262.0 and 21445.0 respectively. Its memory subsystem delivers a read-only large block bandwidth of 244.57 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 105.85 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 33888.6 and a Redis throughput of 78.59 million SET operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference capabilities are notable, processing 300.35 tokens per second for medium 7B models and 39.13 tokens per second for large 70B models during prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.16xlarge offers a high-density memory-to-core ratio combined with high-frequency processing, reducing the need to scale horizontally for memory-bound applications. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage must be network-attached, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy operations. This server is optimized for memory-intensive and high-compute workloads, including relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, electronic design automation (EDA), and CPU-based machine learning inference.
